# Mathematics: the major (designed, parked)

*Designed 2026-10-08; not scheduled. Course data: `curriculum.json` (generated by `scripts/build_majors.py`); the picture:
`DAG.md`. Shape follows `notes/major-design.md`. Course syllabi get written when a course is about to start.*

## TL;DR
- **What it is:** a pure-math major from precalculus to the graduate core (algebra, measure theory, complex analysis, topology,
  then functional analysis, manifolds and algebraic topology).
- **Written for a high-school graduate** (start: MA100 Precalculus). **Your entry point** skips the courses your math degree
  covered (the Applied Mathematics option, plus complex analysis) and starts at **MA435 (abstract algebra I: groups) and
  MA429 (topology)**, plus a retake of MA412 (Fourier series and PDEs). Then MA437 (rings, fields, Galois) finishes Level I's core. Drawn in `DAG.md`.
- **No pretests.** Credited courses come from your transcript; when a gap shows mid-course, you ask or look it up.
- **Size from your entry point:** about 62 lessons of Level I core: three courses (≈ 1.2 years as a half subject at one
  lesson a week, ≈ 0.6 years as a full subject). Level II core is another ≈ 198 lessons. Computed by `build_majors.py --stats`.
- **Books:** almost everything is in your library; Level II needs Dummit & Foote, Folland, Munkres, Kreyszig and Lee.

## 1. Plan
**Why (draft; correct it in MISSION.md):** a "good for the soul" major that finishes what the math degree started (the
proof-based upper division) and goes on into graduate mathematics, with no exam deadline.

**Shape.** Three phases. (1) The computational base every STEM major shares: precalculus, calculus I–III, matrices, ODEs and
probability. These courses are cross-listed with Physics, Mechanical Engineering and Unified Engineering, so one finish counts
in all of them. (2) The proof core: proofs (Velleman), analysis (Abbott, then Rudin), algebra (Artin, all of it), abstract linear
algebra (Axler), complex analysis (Bak & Newman) and topology (Sutherland). (3) Level II, opt-in: the graduate core a qualifying
exam covers, then manifolds and algebraic topology.

**Course numbers follow Penn State's** (MATH 140, 141, 220, 230, 250, 311W, 312, 403, 414, 421, 429, 435, 436), so your old
transcript maps straight onto the DAG.

**Why these books (judgment).** Artin is grade A in your library and is the one algebra text that teaches groups through symmetry
and linear algebra, which suits someone with an engineering half; Abbott is the standard first analysis book and Rudin the
standard second; Axler is the standard proof-based linear algebra. Stewart and Thomas are in the library only as unreadable
copies, so the calculus courses use OpenStax (free, clean equations on the web edition).

**Where you enter (Penn State BS Mathematics, 2026 bulletin [1]).** Every option requires MATH 140, 141, 220, 230, 250/251,
311W, 312, 414 and 415; those are credited. The rest depends on your option: General adds 403 and one of 435/436; Graduate
Study adds 403, 404, 421, 429, 435 and 436; Applied adds 403, 412, 436 and 455. You did Applied and also took complex
analysis (421) and numerical analysis II (456), so 403, 421, 436 and 455 are credited. PDEs (412) you want to
retake, so MA412 is a start course even though it is an elective here (≈ 18 lessons on top of the core). Applied doesn't require abstract algebra (435) or topology (429),
so those are where the core continues. MA417 (dynamical systems) is "maybe": MATH 417 was one of Applied's elective choices.
The bulletin is today's; your catalog year may differ slightly.

## 3. How it would run (when it starts)
- One lesson = two 25-minute blocks: a reading block (a few pages with a reading guide) and a lesson page with worked examples,
  practice and **one proof you write** (the Statistics format).
- Every lesson ends with **Extra practice (optional)**: numbered exercises from the course's own book, a second-book reading for
  another angle, and one good article (TEACHING-LOG rule 32).
- Review questions come back as **variants**, not the same item (proposal in `notes/practice-variants.md`).
- Overlaps: MA414 is also covered by the Statistics major (Casella & Berger ch. 1–5); MA511 overlaps Statistics S501.
